blindSummary:
This state/province is the only jurisdiction in the country to pass laws targeting transgender people as a class and then shield those laws from judicial review. Three bills, announced in January 2024 and enacted in December 2024: a 2024 education amendment act requires parental notification/consent before staff use a student's gender-related preferred name or pronouns (in full force since 1 September 2025); a 2024 health amendment act prohibits puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and a vital-statistics rule was amended. A 2025 government bill invoked the constitution's override clause over all three laws, and after it passed, a provincial trial-court judge lifted the injunction that had been pausing the care ban; a government appeal then succeeded, removing the injunction. Two national 2SLGBTQ+ organisations, with five gender-diverse youth, continue a constitutional challenge despite the shield ("the fight isn't over").

These school and healthcare provisions are primarily resident-facing and carry small traveler-facing weight. The more directly relevant signal is the documented street-level pattern in the state/province's second-largest city: from 2023 a pastor led repeated disruptions of library drag-storytime events - charging into a library classroom and shouting homophobic and transphobic slurs at parents and children, who left crying - and the litigation has run for years: a conviction for harassing a library worker was upheld on appeal, acquittals on disturbance and mischief charges were overturned with a new trial ordered, and a further breach conviction followed in 2026. Reporting from March 2023 noted many drag events cancelled or postponed citywide as threats and protests escalated. The pairing of trans-targeting legislation, a judicial-override shield and a documented event-cancellation pattern marks a clear hardening of official posture.
blindSourceSummaries: National public broadcaster (4 December 2024): the trio of bills in this state/province affecting transgender people - pronoun/parental-notification opt-ins in schools, the ban on gender-affirming care for minors, and a vital-statistics change - passed the legislature's final stage; 2SLGBTQ+ advocacy groups say they will continue legal action.

National public broadcaster (December 2025): the 2025 override bill shielded the three transgender-affecting laws from legal action; a national equality organisation and a trans-community legal group, with five gender-diverse youth, say they will continue the court challenge of the care-ban law regardless ("the fight isn't over").

National public broadcaster: an appellate court upholds a pastor's conviction for harassing a library worker during his disruptions of library drag-storytime events in this state/province's second-largest city, part of years of litigation over the protest pattern.

National public broadcaster: the same pastor's acquittals on disturbing-the-peace and mischief charges over a library drag-reading protest are overturned on appeal and new trials are ordered, extending the drag-event court saga.

Independent LGBTQ2S+ magazine (March 2023): within "a rising tide of anti-LGBTQ2S+ and anti-drag protests" in this state/province's second-largest city, a pastor was charged after aggressively entering a library classroom and shouting homophobic and transphobic slurs at parents and children at a drag storytime event; police describe several people scaring children and refusing to leave, and note many drag events cancelled or postponed citywide as threats escalated.
blindOutOfScope: This state/province's second-highest sub-national 2021 gender-related homicide rate of women and girls (0.68 per 100,000) is a general gendered-violence base-rate proxy, not a trans-specific measure; it does not belong in a trans-traveller assessment.
blindLocalsOnly: The school pronoun/opt-in rules, the minors' care ban and the vital-statistics amendment bind residents' institutions - a visitor uses their home passport and never touches them; their traveller-facing weight is the climate signal and the street pattern, not the letter of the laws.
